Special Council Meeting
CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
ACTION AGENDA
The Action Agenda of the City Council Meeting is a document provided immediately following the Council Meeting in order for staff and the public to be aware of the business transacted and actions taken by Council. This is a preliminary draft and not a public record. The meeting's legal record is the Minutes approved by the City Council.
SOLANA BEACH CITY COUNCIL
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY and PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY

6:00 P.M.
Special
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
NOTICE
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, persons with a disability may request an agenda in appropriate alternative formats as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990. Any person with a disability who requires a modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should direct such request to the City Clerk's office at (858) 720-2400 or by email at least 72 hours before the meeting.
As a courtesy to all meeting attendees, please set cellular phones and pagers to silent mode and engage in conversations outside the Council Chambers.
The Regular Meetings of the City Council are scheduled for the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays and are broadcast live on Cox Communications, Channel 19, and Time Warner, Channel 24. Council meetings are archived and available for viewing. The video taping of meetings are maintained as a permanent record and contain a detailed account of the proceedings.
A full City Council agenda packet with backup information is available at City Hall, at the Solana Beach branch of the San Diego County Library (157 Stevens Ave.), and online www.ci.solana-beach.ca.us at least 72 hours prior to the meeting. Agenda related writings or documents regarding an agenda item and that are received after the distribution of the agenda but at least 1 hour 30 minutes prior to the meeting will be available for public viewing at City Hall and posted online with the agenda.

Special Council Meeting
CITY OF SOLANA BEACH
Special Council Meeting
Solana Beach City Council, Redevelopment Agency, and Public Financing Authority
MINUTES
JOINT SPECIAL MEETING
Tuesday, December 9, 2008
06:00 P.M.
Special
The City Council acts as the City of Solana Beach Redevelopment Agency and the Public Financing Authority.
CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL:
Mayor Roberts called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.
Present:
Roberts, Nichols, Campbell, Heebner, and Kellejian.
Absent:
None.
Also Present:
David Ott, City Manager
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney
Angela Ivey, City Clerk
Wende Protzman, Deputy City Mgr/ Dir. Admin Services
Dennis Coleman, Finance Director
Mo Sammak, City Engineer/Dir. Public Works
Tina Christiansen, Community Development Dir.
FLAG SALUTE:
Deputy Mayor Nichols led the flag salute.
Mayor Roberts stated that Reverend Reese had passed away in October and was a long term resident and active member of the Civic and Historical Society. He said that he would like to adjourn the meeting in his memory.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA:
MOTION: Moved by Nichols and seconded by Heebner.
Motion carried unanimously.
COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENTS:
Council reported community announcements.
COMMENTARY:
PRESENTATIONS:
(Ceremonial items that do not contain in-depth discussion and no action/direction.)
1.
I-5 Interchange
David Ott, City Manager, stated that the presentation was a focus on the Santa Helena area and improvements that were coming.
Mo Sammak, presented a Powerpoint, stating it was an informational presentation regarding the project specifically the right hand lane on Lomas Santa Fe onto Santa Helena. He reviewed the background of what it used to look like with an exclusive right hand lane turn onto the Santa Helena and the signage that showed the lane requiring all traffic in that lane to turn right rather than proceeding onto the area towards the freeway. He showed the changes coming to allow traffic to move forward to the lanes that would feed to the on ramp. He stated that a traffic analysis provided input on the benefits on the changes which would enhance the movement of the traffic and create a shorter signal cycle.
David Ott, City Manager, added clarification and stated that the light would be moved shortening the signal light and that the traffic eastbound or westbound would have to go on one ramp which would increase the capacity off of Lomas Santa Fe by up to 70%.
City Engineer and City Manager discussed traffic signal cycle times, study results, auxiliary lanes, Caltrans recommendation regarding the crossing of traffic off of Santa Helena, RBFs videotaping of cars stacking on Santa Helena would still enter the street in no more than one signal light cycle.
Council and staff discussio ensued regarding why Caltrans would not allow the Santa Helena right hand only lane continue to exist due to traffic feeding onto freeway traffic, bicycle traffic, that the freeway tunnel would be lit for cars and pedestrians, and that the project should be finished in January sometime.

CONSENT CALENDAR: (Action Items)
Items listed on the Consent Calendar are to be acted in a single action of the City Council unless pulled for discussion.
Any member of the public may address the City Council on an item of concern by submitting to the City Clerk a speaker slip
(located on the back table) before the Consent Calendar is addressed.
Those items removed from the Consent Calendar by a member of the Council will be trailed to the end of the agenda,
while Consent Calendar items removed by the public will be discussed immediately after approval of
the Consent Calendar.

1.
Approve the Minutes of the Regular City Council meeting held May 27, 2008.

Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Adopt Resolution 2008-189:
a.
Accepting $160,000 from Caltrans, via Coffman Specialties, for the installation of mosaic artwork on retaining walls constructed as part of the Interchange project and appropriating the same amount to Miscellaneous Income in the Lomas Santa Fe at I-5 Interchange Project (459-4850-9356.01-4850).
b.
Appropriating $160,000 to the Lomas Santa Fe at I-5 Interchange Project, Expenditure Budget Unit 459-9356-6510-6530, Project No. 9356.01-6661.

NOTE: The City Council shall not begin a new agenda item after 10:30 p.m. unless approved by a unanimous vote of all members present. (SBMC 2.04.070)
B.
PUBLIC HEARINGS:
This portion of the agenda provides citizens an opportunity to express their views on a specific issue as required by law
after proper noticing by submitting a speaker slip (located on the back table) to the City Clerk .
After considering all of the evidence, including written materials and oral testimony,
the City Council must make a decision supported by findings and the findings must be supported by substantial evidence in the record.
An applicant or designees for a private development/business project, for which the public hearing is being held,
is allotted a total of fifteen minutes to speak, as per SBMC 2.04.210. A portion of the fifteen minutes may be saved to respond to those who speak in opposition.
All other speakers have three minutes each. Please be aware of the timer light on the Council Dais.
B.1.
Emergency Request for Conditional Use Permit for Coastal Bluff Stabilization at 365 Pacific (Applicant: Bennett Bloom), 367 Pacific (Applicant: Kari De Burgh), 371 Pacific (Applicant: John Cumming) (Case No: 17-08-16) (File 0610-10)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Report Council disclosures.
2.
Conduct the Public Hearing: Open the public hearing, Receive public testimony, Close the public hearing.
3.
Find the project exempt from the requirements of CEQA pursuant to 2008 State California CEQA Guidelines Section 15269(b) as a documented emergency
exists.
4.
Adopt Resolution 2008-128 conditionally approving an emergency request for a Conditional Use Permit to reconstruct and stabilize the existing seawall along the bluffs below 365-371 Pacific Avenue.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Leslea Meyerhoff, consultant, presented a powerpoint.
Council and consultant discussed the reference to changing something that looks natural to be more natural, the concern that that the contour could be less engineered and more natural, and that they are designed to be removable.
Walt Crampton, pyrotechnical engineer, Terra Costa, explained the removable strand tie back.
Mayor Roberts opened the public hearing.
Council disclosed their familiarity with the project.
Walt Crampton, engineer, representative for the applicant, presented a powerpoint. He reviewed some background which included the residence at 371 Pacific which was approved in the past and considered the complete area to infill but was not completed since not everyone could afford it, that a storm season had continued to make the situation a plaquing issue, and that several surrounding issues are related and interconnected.
MOTION: Moved by Heebner and seconded by Campbell to closed the public hearing.
Motion carried unanimously.
MOTION: Moved by Heebner and seconded by Kellejian to approve with modifications.
Motion carried unanimously.
Deputy Mayor Nichols asked about backfill of material to engineer the slope and how far back it was allowed to encroach back.
Staff and consultant explained that the City's ordinance allows for walls to be restored to the 1991 level and that the proposed project was designed to restore the bluff a few feet westward to the 2001 contour in order to hold up the concrete patio.
C.
STAFF REPORTS:
Submit speaker slips to the City Clerk
C.1.
La Colonia Park & Community Center Conceptual Design Presentation. (File 0400-10)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Receive the report from Van Dyke Landscape Architects and City staff.
2.
Provide direction on moving forward with the project based on one of the options presented or combination thereof.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Steve Didier, Assistant to the City Manager, presented a Powerpoint, reviewing the needs assessment and community outreach events.
Beth Bowen and Mitch Phillipe, VanDyke Landscape Architects, continued the Powerppoint and reviewed the three Master Plan Options.
Jim Nelson, read a letter by Judy Hegenauer of the Civic and Historical Society, which stated that the Society had maintained and furnished the museum for a long time and was interested in the ultimate location, that it supported Option 1 since it maintained the location of the building, that they opposed Option 2 due to lack of visilbity and parking, that Option 3 would be supported with modifications to support visbibility, accessibility and functionality, that if Option 3 were selected they would prefer to have turf in the outdoor area, that the placement of shed in Option 3 was unclear. Mr. Nelson added his own comments that the Society did not envision using an outside area since they would utilize the San Dieguito outdoor area, that he would favor mirroring the design of the ranch house, and that the front door of the shed be placed in the same plane as the front door of the museum.
Council and Mr. Nelson discussed the front door, activities, they the Society had not talked with the landscape architects, and that the Society had a split vote between Option 1 and 3.
Tara Gordon referenced Jim Nelson’s book "Early Solana Book" who was a member of the spec about mural and art at La Colonia. She offered two suggestions, first was to incorporate art and design from into the proposals from the beginning and to utilize Jim Nelson’s book for a mural that would depict scenes of early Solana Beach.
Council and staff discussed whether this project would be subject to the 1/2 of the 1% art fee and to consider utilizing the M.A.P. (Master Art Policy) process.
Jim Nelson stated that Tara Gordan attended the Society’s Board meeting, that there was a vote to support her suggestions, that Betsy Schultz had done a superb job of tracing the history of Solana Beach in the arches on the Coastal Rail Trail, and that the Society would like any art to reinforce that the building and park is a community facility.
Council, staff and consultants discussed assigning a subcommittee to this issue, that the consideration of a skate park would reduce the size of the playing field by approximately 10%, that the playing field was be smaller than a full size regulation field, to have the Sheriff look at the options for safety issues, the potential lighting options, and the size of the skate park to meet needs.
Beth Bowen, VanDyke, stated that the designer did create small scale skate areas, that they spoke with various skate kids and partners to develop this design, 5500 sq ft and would accommodate the kids we met, skate designers opinion
Council, staff and consultants discussion ensued regarding several positive comments from the community in regards to their discussions with VanDyke, that one of the highest requested items was a skate park, to highly consider the Civic and Historical Society’s requests, that the cost per acre at Fletcher Cove was 1.2 million and proposed at La Colonia for Option 2 & 3 would be 1.1 million,
Steve Didier, Assistant to the City Manager, stated that they would take the feedback from this evening and prepare one more design view and return to Council one more time.
Council and staff discussed using a phasing document for planning and affordability, whether it needed to financed for the future, and that there was most consensus for Option 3 with some ideas from this evening's discussion.
Mayor Nichols recessed the meeting for a break at 8:30 p.m. and reconvened at 8:35 p.m.
C.2.
Council Policy 17 Master Art Policy Revisions. (File 0410-90)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Adopt Resolution 2008-187 approving proposed revisions to City Council Policy No.17 - Master Art Policy.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Steve Didier, Management Analyst, presented a Powerpoint presentation.
Council discussion ensued regarding the acceptance of art donations, whether all donations had to go through the Public Arts Advisory Commission (PAAC), that donations that did not have to go through the PAAC if they did not involve a public site location, that Council had the ability to reject, accept or provide alternative direction to the Arts Commssion, and whether public comments would be confidential prior to Council decision.
David Ott, City Manager, stated that the coments would be private until the item went before Council, that it was a way to prevent undue influence of the process, and that the comments would be public once they were reviewed by Council.
Council discussion ensued with staff regarding the 45 day review period, that the comments were not public until the end of the review period, that having the comments private during the review period would allow for a more fair outcome due to others not influencing the outcome, that some Councilmembers had concerns about transparency and the democratic process, that the comments would become public after the review period, that the identity of who submitted the comment would not be public, and that comments could be deciphiered by the handwriting and personal information included in them.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, stated that the comments would become public upon presentation to the Council, that the identity of the author would only be protected during the 45 day comment period but the comment would still be public, that the comments for the art were different from comments submitted for a Development Review Permit (DRP) because the DRP process was a quasi-judicial function, and that those decisions were based on information provided at the time of the hearing.
Council discussion ensued with staff regarding public comments provided for agenda items, why public art would be different from other items, that this would be a proposed policy, that the comments would be subject to the Public Records Act, that the comments would be provided upon a public records request, and that not disclosing the names on the public art comments until the end of the review period would be a Council policy decision.
Council discussion ensued on the confidentiality of public comments, that citizens had difficulty making negative comments regarding art, that protecting names would allow more people to comment and feel more comfortable, and whether there could be an option to remain anonymous.
Council and staff discussion ensued regarding public records, that the comments could not be protected under the Act even during the 45 day review period, and that the City would have to provide the documents if requested.
Council discussion ensued with staff regarding permanent v. temporary art, whether there would be another revision on the document to include temporary art, that art could either be permanent or temporary, whether the subcommittee had discussed temporary v. permaent art, and that this policy was only for permanent art.
Council discussion ensued regarding their intent to have names private to make it more comfortable for people to comment, and that due to the Public Records Act, it would not be possible to protect the identity of the authors, so people would have to comment knowing that their comment could be released.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, stated that the City could not require people to provide contact information on public comments, that other cities tended to weigh anonymous comments less since there was no contact informaiton available to contact the individual.
Council discussion ensued regarding changes that had been discussed to the document at this meeting, that the final document should come back to council, that it would be difficult to determine the significance of a memorial, and how those determinations would be made.
Council discussion ensued regarding taking the document back to the subcommittee, staff revising the document based on this dicussion and returning to council at a later date, that the subcommittee could review other cities' policies on how determinations were made for memorials, and that staff should continue to review this section for clarity.
C.3.
Extension Request for Development Review and Structure Development Permits at 614 Mar Vista Dr. (Case 17-06-12, Applicant: Ryan Gonzales). (File 0600-40)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Grant the request for an extension beginning on November 8, 2008 to set a final expiration date of November 8, 2010 for the approval of 17-06-12 DRP/SDP for the construction of a new 3,838 square foot (including garage), two-story residence on property at 614 Mar Vista Drive.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Corey Johnson, Assistant Planner, presented a Powerpoint.
Council and staff discussed the criteria used to grant extensions by the Municipal Code and that extensions may be granted up to two years at Council’s discretion but that it was silent about how many times it may be granted.
Gary Martin, additional time donated by Julie Brown, stated that he wanted to talk about how Council exercises extensions, asked what the criteria was for Council to make the determination, that the length of an extension should be supported by facts in the record, and that the letter submitted deals with what has happed in the past but what will be done in the future should be considered in order to reasonably justify an extension.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, stated that upon further review that code clearly states "an extension" so it appears to focus on a singular extension and therefore she would have to determine that one extension would be allowed for up to two years. She said she could do further research to determine the intentional design of the code if Council requested.
Council discussed concerns regarding setting a precedent and the interest in seeing a plan from the applicant of what would be done to get the project built during an extension.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, stated that Council was required to determine findings under this section of whether there were no significant changes to the General Plan, Zoning Ordinance, or character of the area within the area of which the project is located that would cause the approved proejct to become inconsistent or nonconforming and whether the granting of the extension would be detrimental to the health, safety or welfare or materially injurist to properties or improvements in the vicinity. She said that these were the two findings that Council needed to satisfy.
Deputy Mayor Nichols stated that he did not have a problem with the extension but with a larger case in the future that could be a concern, that this person was under the current ordinance, that the big picture was what to do in the future, that revisions are necessary for the futurefor clarity and suggested that it be brought back for changes in the future.
Council and City Manager discussed what ideas of criteria including providing good faith timeline, providing what the applicant was going to do to complete the project, provide a realistic timeline, and whether granting one extension sets a precedent.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, answered that it would not set a precedence since each item is based on the facts presented at that time and that no situation is the same.
Mayor Roberts stated that he could not vote on this item at this time.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, stated that the law would require that the existing ordinance would stay in place until a new ordinance would take its place.
Councilmember Campbell stated this was a matter of exercising discretion, that that Code says that the Council may grant and not that it shall grant, and that he needed the plan and the problem in order to exercise this discretion.
Mayor Roberts stated that he could not support the extension until he could get the information to the questions.
MOTION: Moved by Roberts and seconded by Campbell to continue to the January 14, 2009 meeting returing with answers to the posed questions.
Motion carried 4/1
(Noes: Kellejian.)
